John Leslie Pollock, born on January 28, 1940, earned degrees in physics, mathematics, and philosophy from the University of Minnesota in 1961. His doctoral dissertation from the University of California, Berkeley, involved an appendix on defeasible reasoning, which became a major contribution to his philosophical work.
Pollock became recognized in philosophy as an expert in "Mr. Defeasible Reasoning" due to his early commitment to this concept. His work established his presence in epistemology through the book *Knowledge and Justification* (1974). Later in his career, he devoted time to OSCAR, a LISP-based AI software prototype embodying his ideas on defeasible reasoning, intentions, and problem-solving. He also investigated the relationship between defeasible reasoning and probability in his 1990 work, *Nomic Probability and The Foundations of Induction* .
